draft.title: Mass and energy
card: E = mc² links a mass m to an energy E. The speed of light c is very large, so a small mass is equal to a huge amount of energy. Mass is a form of energy.
If a system's mass changes, its energy changes by ΔE = Δm c². In nuclear reactions, a small loss of mass is released as a large amount of energy.
Relativistic momentum is p = γmv, where γ is the Lorentz factor. As speed v gets close to c, γ becomes very large, so p grows without limit.
Giving an object more and more momentum takes more and more energy. No finite amount is enough to reach c, so nothing with mass can reach the speed of light.
draft.remember: Mass is energy, and momentum grows without limit near c, so mass cannot reach c.

a.q: A nuclear reaction releases energy and the total mass of the products is slightly less than the mass before. What explains this?
opts: Some of the mass was changed into energy
The energy released had no source in the reaction
Mass is always conserved as a separate quantity
The products moved faster than the speed of light
a.why: Mass is a form of energy, so a loss of mass Δm is released as energy ΔE = Δm c². Saying mass is always conserved on its own is wrong here, because the missing mass appears as energy.
a.clue: Where does the energy come from if mass is a form of energy?

b.q: A proton in a particle accelerator is given more and more energy, and its speed gets closer to c. Why can it never reach c?
opts: Its momentum would have to become infinitely large
Its mass would drop to zero as it nears c
Its kinetic energy stops increasing near c
Its Lorentz factor becomes smaller as it speeds up
b.why: Momentum is p = γmv, and γ grows without limit as v nears c. Reaching c would need infinite momentum and so infinite energy. The tempting idea that energy stops increasing is wrong: the energy keeps rising, but speed gains get tiny.
b.clue: Think about what happens to γ as v approaches c.

a.best: Some of the mass was changed into energy

b.best: Its momentum would have to become infinitely large

problems.detail: "mass cannot reach c" is loose: it is objects with mass that cannot reach c, as the card says ("nothing with mass can reach the speed of light"). "Mass is energy" also overstates the card's "Mass is a form of energy".

check.summary: The physics and both questions are correct, with a single right answer each. The remember line is loosely worded: it says "mass cannot reach c" rather than "nothing with mass can reach c", and "Mass is energy" overstates the card's "a form of energy".
